account:
It is eleven on day zero, and so far the town appears to be following its ordinary routines. I spent the morning dealing with my appointment book and walking through the plaza market. The secretary borrowed the book to review my schedule and prepare meetings, then returned it to the appointments chest. She said there was no correspondence or urgent news. Two residents I asked, Townsfolk 08 and Townsfolk 30, reported no news. I bought a fresh loaf baked today from the bakery stall for one emerald. Nothing I have seen establishes a problem with supplies or town business.

The neighbour is now at the plaza and has confirmed our usual tea at their cottage at three. I asked whether that is the cottage near the east ferry landing at coordinates sixteen, one hundred and five, but have not yet heard confirmation. The cottage's exact location remains uncertain. I also overheard Townsfolk 30 talking while approaching the plaza, but could not make out the words, so I cannot say what that conversation concerned. I have noticed nothing clearly unusual and have no evidence of any hidden undertaking. My remaining scheduled business is lunch at home at noon, office accounts at one, tea at three, office at four thirty, and home at seven.
